content.value_statement: Cloudflare One deployments span identity, traffic, devices, private networks, and data controls. This skill structures design, configuration, troubleshooting, validation, and staged rollout decisions.
actual_capabilities: Classifies requests as architecture, configuration, troubleshooting, migration, or review work.
Collects relevant identity, application, device, routing, compliance, and rollout requirements.
Designs Access, Gateway, WARP, Tunnel, Mesh, DLP, CASB, and Cloudflare WAN changes.
Explains policy evaluation, private routing, split tunnels, TLS inspection, and device enrollment dependencies.
Provides validation tests, evidence checks, staged rollout guidance, and rollback considerations.
Directs users to current Cloudflare documentation before citing mutable limits, fields, or interface paths.
limitations: It requires current Cloudflare documentation for exact limits, fields, category identifiers, and interface paths.
It cannot inspect or change an account unless authorized tools and account access are available.
Migration planning from another vendor belongs to the separate cloudflare-one-migrations skill.
Final configuration choices depend on account entitlements, topology, identity data, and compliance requirements.

use_cases.title: Plan a Zero Trust rollout
use_cases.description: Create a phased Cloudflare One architecture with prerequisites, pilot scope, validation, and rollback.

use_cases.title: Configure private application access
use_cases.description: Map Access policies, device enrollment, routes, DNS resolution, and tunnel redundancy for private applications.

use_cases.title: Diagnose policy failures
use_cases.description: Trace Access, Gateway, DNS, device client, or tunnel failures from logs toward the responsible configuration.

prompt_templates.title: Review my deployment
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Cloudflare One deployment for [users, sites, and applications]. Identify missing context, major risks, and next validation steps.

prompt_templates.title: Design private access
prompt_templates.prompt: Design private access for [applications] from [devices and sites]. Include identity, enrollment, tunnels, routes, DNS, pilot scope, tests, and rollback.

prompt_templates.title: Troubleshoot blocked traffic
prompt_templates.prompt: Troubleshoot [traffic failure]. Use these logs and settings: [evidence]. Map the traffic path, likely failure point, next test, and corrective action.

prompt_templates.title: Plan layered controls
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a staged Access, Gateway, TLS, and DLP design for [requirements]. Compare policy interactions, exceptions, monitoring, tests, and rollback gates.

output_examples.input: Design private application access for managed employees and unmanaged contractors.
output_examples.output: Use device-client private routing for managed employees and clientless access where supported for contractors. Define separate policies, pilot groups, tests, and rollback.

output_examples.input: Why does a healthy tunnel not reach my private application?
output_examples.output: Tunnel health confirms connector reachability only. Verify published routes, split tunnel alignment, private DNS resolution, origin reachability, Access policy, and relevant logs.

output_examples.input: Prepare a safe TLS inspection rollout.
output_examples.output: Deploy the trusted root certificate, inventory pinned applications, create inspection exceptions, enable a limited pilot, monitor failures, then expand through approval gates.

best_practices: Retrieve current documentation before using exact limits, identifiers, API fields, or interface paths.
Inspect existing resources and dependencies before proposing account changes.
Stage risky policies disabled or within a pilot, then validate expected and denied flows before expansion.
anti_patterns: Do not invent application identifiers, category identifiers, policy fields, or request bodies.
Do not enable broad production inspection or blocking without explicit approval and tested rollback.
Do not treat tunnel health, routes, DNS, enrollment, and authorization as interchangeable signals.

faq.question: Can this skill make Cloudflare account changes?
faq.answer: Only when authorized account tools are available. It first inspects existing resources and proposes staged changes with validation and rollback.

faq.question: Does it support Access and Gateway?
faq.answer: Yes. It distinguishes application authorization through Access from traffic inspection and filtering through Gateway.

faq.question: Can it design private network access?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers tunnels, routes, private DNS, device clients, split tunnels, Access policies, redundancy, and origin reachability.

faq.question: Does it cover DLP and TLS inspection?
faq.answer: Yes. It addresses certificate deployment, inspection exceptions, DLP profiles, payload logging, testing, and staged enforcement.

faq.question: Can it migrate from another security vendor?
faq.answer: Use the separate cloudflare-one-migrations skill for vendor migration planning. This skill handles Cloudflare One design and operations.

faq.question: How does it keep guidance current?
faq.answer: It retrieves relevant Cloudflare documentation or API schemas before citing mutable limits, settings, fields, identifiers, or interface paths.
